datasets.title: IOM Bangladesh - Needs and Population Monitoring (NPM) Majhee Blocks Mapping
datasets.description: The majhee block system represents an important aspect of communities within the Rohingya refugees settled in collective or camp-like settings in Cox's Bazar district. A majhee is a community leader belonging to the Rohingya refugee population, while a block is the area for which he is responsible. The NPM majhee blocks mapping exercise was first conducted during NPM Baseline 9, between 5 and 20 February 2018. As part of the majhee interview process (key informants), enumerators walked the perimeter of each majhee block with guidance from the KI. As they walked, the field team traced their path, marking up the boundary on the tablet or paper map. Upon returning to NPM office, details of these boundaries were finalized on the paper maps. The paper maps were then received by the NPM digitizing team. This team carefully digitized the Mahjee zone perimeters in GIS, using high-resolution NPM UAV imagery as an underlying reference. Boundaries were assigned the NPM Block_ID attribute, which represents a unique identifier for each Site Assessment Location. In this manner, boundaries can be uniquely linked back to a mahjee. The majhee blocks mapping exercise is now embedded in NPM regular assessment activities (baseline and site assessment), hence regularly updated with a frequency of approximately three weeks. The majhee block system is not an official form of governance. The scope of this exercise is purely descriptive and not prescriptive. Names and boundaries adopted in this exercise do not imply official endorsement or acceptance by IOM.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/iom-bangladesh-needs-and-population-monitoring-npm-majhee-blocks-mapping]

entity.name: International Organization for Migration (IOM) - Needs and Population Monitoring (NPM)

lineage.description: NPM baseline and subsequent monitoring rounds (R9-R15, February 2018 - June 2019) collected spatial boundaries of majhee blocks through participatory mapping with community leaders as key informants. Field teams traced block perimeters and recorded household and population counts within each administrative unit. Data was compiled into shapefile format with temporal snapshots across multiple monitoring rounds.

sources.description: Direct observational enumeration of refugee population and households through key informant interviews with majhee community leaders, with field teams walking block perimeters to delineate spatial boundaries of administrative units.
